provenance.orgName: Sheen, Surrey. Charterhouse of Jesus of Bethlehem

p.q: Liber domus Jhesu de bethleem de scheene ordinis carthusiensis quem scripsit domnus Johannes Whetham monachus professus domus londoniensis eiusdem ordinis pro venerabili patre d. Radulpho Tracy tunc priore dicte domus de Scheene, ad instancias Reverendi patris & domini J. yngylby tunc episcopi Landavensis, qui etiam quondam fuit prior de scheene & predecessor immediatus predicti patris Radulphi Tracy a. d. 1496 Ad laudem dei. Amen.

history.provenance: Duke of Sussex (d. 1843). Sold 31 July 1844 as lot 203: see J. Pettigrew, Bibliotheca Sussexiana, lat. 49.
Ashburnham: see Historical MSS Commission Report, 8, iii.104, no. 78: sold at Ashburnham sale, 1899, lot. 61. Bought by H. W. Underdown.
Tregaskis, Catalogue, 1000 (1931), no. 117, with facsimile, and Catalogue, 1022.
Sotheby's, 26-29 April 1937, lot 252, sold to Maggs for £21.

Rt. Hon. John Burns, sold on his death at Sotheby's, 24 April 1944, lot 424. Subsequenlty owned b A. G. Hinds of Richmond, and then by W. L. Wood of Chandlers Cross. This was the location reported in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964).

Sotheby's, 10 December 1969, lot 80 (Schoenberg 3007). Bought by the dealer Traylen, Catalogue, 81 (1970?), no. 11. This was the last known provenance according to the supplement to Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1987). The book remains untraced.

recordHist.source: Neil R. Ker, ed., Medieval Libraries of Great Britain: A List of Surviving Books, Royal Historical Society Guides and Handbooks, 3 (London, 1941; 2nd edn, 1964; supplement, ed. Andrew G. Watson, 1987; digital edn, ed. Richard Sharpe and James M. W. Willoughby, 2010–15).
